transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump will campaign in South Carolina today
for Republican candidates, including Senator Darlene Graham.
It's a close race with Democrat Annie Andrews.
Former President Barack Obama was
in neighboring Georgia yesterday,
stumping for Democrats.
NPR's Stephen Fowler says this year,
Democrats are stressing issues of affordability.
>> It's a little bit different than the 2018 midterms,
and it's not just an anti-Trump message,
because there's also been an acknowledgment of sorts
that during the Biden administration,
things were also expensive,
and that people who voted for Trump could be kind of forgiven
for believing that a new administration would fix it.
We have polling to back this up, too.
Voters tell us affordability is a top concern,
that the Republican Party and Trump are unpopular,
and that voters think Democrats
would be better than Republicans at handling these issues.
>> NPR's Stephen Fowler reporting.
Houthi rebels in Yemen have been firing missiles
at an airport in southern Yemen
used by international relief groups.
NPR's Aya Batrawi reports the airport is run
by Saudi-backed forces that are fighting the Houthi rebels.
>> The Iran-backed Houthis issued warnings for people
to evacuate the airport in the southern city of Aden,
saying it was being used by a Saudi military cargo plane
to transport weapons into the country.
Soon after the warning, the Saudi-backed Yemeni government
said the Houthis shelled the airport.
It says this is the sixth attack on Aden's airport
in recent days.
The aid group Doctors Without Borders
says these attacks have forced delays at the airport
and described it as the main entry point
for humanitarian workers and aid entering southern Yemen.
Meanwhile, the Houthis say Saudi is launching dozens
of airstrikes daily on Yemen,
and that Saudi strikes killed more than a dozen people
around a market in the northern province of al-Jauf on Wednesday.
Saudi Arabia says it's intercepted more Houthi missiles
targeting its capital, Riyadh.
Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
>> Brazil's defeated presidential candidate
says he is the country's true leader.
Flavio Bolsonaro flew to Miami with his family yesterday.
They were granted U.S. visas.
NPR's Kerry Khan has more.
>> Bolsonaro left Brazil, crossed into Argentina,
then flew to Ecuador and finally to the U.S.
with his family.
He posted a letter on X declaring himself as,
quote, "the true elected president of Brazil."
Not long after, he posted a new statement
downgrading himself to the true elected leader of Brazil.
He compared himself to liberation figures Charles de Gaulle
and Maria Corina Machado of Venezuela, amongst others.
He said he would, from afar, lead the opposition
to incumbent President Luis Anacio Lula da Silva
and accused Brazil's judiciary of being weaponized
to politically persecute his family.
He did not provide evidence of voter fraud.
International observers have commended
Brazil's election results.
Kerry Khan, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.
>> This is NPR.
Spanish authorities say the death toll is at 68 people
from yesterday's train crash in central Spain.
That number may still rise.
A high-speed train collided with the back
of a second train that was stopped.
Officials have indicated one of the trains was given
incorrect instructions.
In the U.S., labor rights activist Dolores Huerta
died yesterday at home in Bakersfield, California.
The 96-year-old was instrumental in improving rights
for farm workers and women.
From member station KVPR, Amre Alvarez visited a mural
of the late activist in her hometown.
>> The mural features Huerta shouting
into a rainbow-colored megaphone.
Flowers and candles were placed in front of it.
Huerta is remembered for her famous protest chant,
"Sí, se puede. Yes, we can."
Manpreet Karr is the vice mayor of Bakersfield.
She says Huerta paved the way for women of color.
>> As an elected official, a woman in public office,
it feels a little bit lonelier knowing that Dolores
isn't there to pull us up onto the stage and say,
"Yes, you can."
>> Earlier this year, Huerta publicly accused
late civil rights leader Cesar Chavez of sexual assault.
Other women have come forward with allegations.
For NPR News, I'm Amre Alvarez in Bakersfield.
>> Game six of the WNBA finals will be held today
just after noon Eastern time.
The Atlanta Dream will host the Golden State Valkyries.
The Valkyries lead the series three to two.
The Atlanta games have all had to be rescheduled
to accommodate last-minute adjustments.
This is NPR.

topics.text: President Trump campaigns in South Carolina for Republican candidates including Senator Darlene Graham
NPR's Stephen Fowler reports Democrats emphasizing affordability in this year's midterm campaigns
Houthi rebels fire missiles at Aden airport in southern Yemen used by aid groups
Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro flees to Miami, claims to be true president
Death toll rises to 68 after high-speed train collision in central Spain
Labor rights activist Dolores Huerta dies at 96 in Bakersfield, California
Game six of WNBA finals set for today, Atlanta Dream host Golden State Valkyries
